subject: Outbound authorization entropy & IP claim — Helix POC
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir.rao@helix-labs.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops-infra@helix-labs.com
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 17:12:00 +0000
Subject: Initial: outbound IP ownership for private endpoint (Helix POC)

Hi Monica / Redwood team,

We're getting close to the Helix POC cutover and security needs confirmation on how Redwood will present egress from the private endpoint. We need a crisp statement of: which IPs you will advertise/claim for the control plane and runtime egress, the expected stability (sticky vs ephemeral), and what proof-of-possession evidence you can provide for our compliance audit.

Current ask: can you provide an "IP claim" artifact and the minimal firewall/allowlist rules Helix should enforce so our perimeter team can sign off? Also note our compliance requires retention of outbound flow evidence for 90 days.

I've attached a short inventory of Helix-side NATs and the initial test plan. Happy to hop on a call if helpful.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Rao
Sr. SRE, Helix Labs

Attachments: helix-nat-inventory.csv (referenced), poc-test-plan.md (referenced)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Rao <samir.rao@helix-labs.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial: outbound IP ownership for private endpoint (Helix POC)

Samir — thanks for the clear ask. Quick answers up front, more detail below.

TL;DR:
- Control plane (management/API): stable set of four static IPs we can reserve and provide; treat those as immutable for firewall rules.
- Runtime (inference tokens): we offer two modes — pinned static egress IPs (recommended for strict allowlists) or ephemeral NAT pools (for scaling). For the POC we suggest pinned static egress to simplify signoff.
- Evidence: we produce an "IP claim manifest" (signed JSON) plus daily egress flow snapshots (jsonlines) for 90 days; those are sufficient for Helix compliance review.

Next steps I propose:
1) David will attach the IP claim ledger and the exact CIDR/IP list.
2) Laura will propose the minimal firewall rule set (ports, SNI, TLS params) for your perimeter.
3) I will run a one-hour handoff with your network/security on Thu.

Notes / constraints / unique items for Helix POC:
- We support TLS 1.3 only for control-plane connections and require SNI to be preserved if Helix uses an egress inspection proxy.
- For static egress IP mode we will bind three candidate IPs per availability zone; those IPs are what we include in the IP claim manifest. If Helix needs single-IP-per-AZ, call that out and we'll allocate.
- Ephemeral mode has "egress entropy": short-lived NAT translations (TTL ~ 5–20 mins) to increase capacity efficiency. That mode complicates allowlisting and evidence collection; not recommended for the POC.

I attached our standard "ip-ledger.csv" snapshot (prelim) and a one-page runbook. If you want the signed manifest earlier, David can push the signed artifact.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Director, Customer Security & Onboarding
Redwood Inference

Attachments: ip-ledger.csv, redwood-egress-runbook-onepage.pdf

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Samir Rao <samir.rao@helix-labs.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial: outbound IP ownership for private endpoint (Helix POC)

Folks — attaching the technical matrix and the signed IP claim manifest. Summary matrix below for quick copy/paste into Helix firewall rules.

Redwood outbound endpoints (POC, static mode):
- Control plane: 34.211.117.22/32, 34.211.117.23/32, 34.211.117.24/32, 34.211.117.25/32 (TCP 443) — management APIs and health checks.
- Runtime inference egress (recommended pinned mode): 54.203.9.128/32 (zone A), 54.203.9.129/32 (zone B), 54.203.9.130/32 (zone C) — TLS 443, SNI: runtime.redwood-inference.com
- Fallback / ephemeral (only if pinned mode not possible): NAT pool 54.203.10.0/24 with TTL-based rotation; evidence snapshots will include mapping tables tied to request IDs.

Firewall rules (minimal):
- Permit outbound TCP 443 to the four control-plane IPs; require SNI runtime.redwood-inference.com for deep-inspection bypass.
- Permit outbound TCP 443 to the three runtime IPs; no other ports required.
- ICMP: denied by default (not required).

Evidence + retention:
- Signed IP claim manifest (attached, sha256 signed)
- Daily egress flow snapshots (jsonl) for 90 days; each record contains timestamp, source private IP, destination public IP, TLS SNI, request_id.
- We can provide on-demand packet-capture hashes for specific incidents (requires mutual NDA for deep capture).

Attachments: egress-proof.pdf (signed manifest + evidence sample), ip-ledger.csv (CSV ledger for rule import).

If Helix wants the rule set as a Palo Alto / Cisco config snippet I can produce that as well — say which firewall make/model and I'll export.

-David
David Kim
Principal Network Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Rao <samir.rao@helix-labs.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2026 23:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Outbound authorization entropy & IP claim — Helix POC

Samir — appreciate the quick review and the clarifying questions on retention. Actionable next steps so we can close the compliance ticket: 

Action items (Helix / Redwood):
- Helix: confirm you want pinned static egress for the POC (single checkbox), and provide firewall appliance vendor/model if you want vendor-specific snippets. (owner: Helix, due: 2026-09-06)
- Redwood (David): convert the IP list into Palo Alto XML snippet and produce the signed IP claim manifest (owner: David, done).
- Redwood (Monica): schedule Thu handoff with Helix network (owner: Monica, scheduled for 2026-09-09 15:00 UTC).
- Helix: confirm retention process (you requested 90 days) — we will push daily jsonl snapshots into your secure S3 bucket or provide access via our evidence portal. Tell us preferred delivery; if S3 we will need a bucket ARN and a cross-account role. (owner: Helix, due: 2026-09-07)

Special note about "egress entropy": if at any point Helix opts into ephemeral NATs for scale, we will include a mapping manifest that correlates request_id -> nat_ip for the retention window, but debugging and allowlisting will be harder. For production-grade customers many choose pinned static egress for predictability and simpler firewall rules.

I'll attach the signed manifest and the export David included for your security team. If anything else is required for audit evidence (e.g., signed attestations on chain-of-custody), escalate to me and I'll engage Legal.

Thanks — see you at the handoff.

Monica Patel
Director, Customer Security & Onboarding
Redwood Inference

Attachments: egress-proof.pdf, ip-ledger.csv
